synopsis: EMESRT PR-5A supplies mining vehicle-interaction scenarios and a nine-layer control model: Level 7 is operator awareness, Level 8 advisory controls, and Level 9 automatic slowing and stopping; several chapters identify Revision 3.0 dated September 2024, although another chapter leaves the current edition uncertain [f2120, f5924, f6231, f4321]. Level 8–9 implementation depends on understanding the Level 1–7 baseline and integrating existing site controls; EMESRT guidance is not itself law or proof of product acceptance, while South African intervention requirements were gazetted on 21 December 2022 [f702, f704, f2586, f2587, f3624]. Scenario counts remain unresolved: a 2019 trade article reports 24 scenarios, whereas EMESRT's 2024 Activity Report reports 17 surface storyboards published in 2019 [f4079]. The storyboards provide useful mining hazard content, but are not machine-readable, cover only expert-envisaged situations, and provide no occurrence frequencies; no equivalent practical general-construction taxonomy was found [f7184, f6755, f6756, f4082]. For a programme starting from zero in October 2026, an ISO 21815-3/EMESRT-mapped operating domain and scenario catalogue is considered realistic by mid-2027, with physical confirmation recommended for at least one run per scenario family [f831, f7887]. These positive findings coexist with planning and skeptic-review passages saying EMESRT controls or leads were not reviewed or verified, so source verification remains an explicit gap [f9808, f11206, f11274].
